answers.value: All change-request artifacts for the release under design assurance: architecture diagrams (C4 model in Confluence space ARCH), pull requests and code-review records in GitHub Enterprise repo, CI test results from the Jenkins pipeline, and the risk log in the GRC platform. Scope = one release train / one Jira epic (e.g. EPIC-1420).
The current release cycle only: from feature-branch cut to release-candidate freeze (e.g. 2026-06-15 through 2026-06-30); evidence dated outside this window is excluded.

Each evidence item carries: source URL/permalink, author, timestamp, and Jira issue key. Architecture diagram version tag present; code-review record shows 2 approvers; test-result artifact shows pass rate and coverage %. Any field blank = item rejected.

Evidence item count reconciles to the assurance checklist: 1 architecture diagram + N code-review records (= N merged PRs in the epic) + 1 CI test-result set + 1 risk-log export. Delta must be 0; any missing item logged as a gap.

All collected evidence uploaded to the compliance evidence repository under folder /assurance/<epic-key>/ with immutable timestamp and version label v<n>; retention 3 years per NYDFS audit-trail requirement.

Missing or stale evidence raised as Jira issue type 'SDLC-Exception', assignee = Engineering Manager, disposition (waiver / remediate / accept-risk) recorded with reason and 10-business-day remediation SLA.

Pre/post comparison: assurance-evidence bundle diffed against the prior release bundle to confirm all mandatory artifact types present and no regressions in coverage or open-risk count; comparison report attached to the change ticket.
Change ticket = ServiceNow CHG record for the release, cross-linked to the Jira epic and the GitHub release tag; ticket URL recorded on the evidence bundle cover sheet.
100% of mandatory assurance artifacts for the epic (architecture diagram, all code-review records, CI results, risk log) — no sampling; census test of the full evidence set.
PASS = all 4 mandatory artifact types present, each with valid version/timestamp and required approvals; 0 items missing. FAIL = any mandatory artifact absent, unversioned, or lacking sign-off.

On FAIL, block the assurance gate, open an 'SDLC-Exception' Jira ticket (owner = Engineering Manager), and either obtain the missing artifact or record an approved waiver before release; 10-business-day remediation SLA.
Field definitions sourced from the assurance-checklist data dictionary in Confluence: artifact_type, source_url, author, timestamp, jira_key, version, approver_count — one row per evidence item.

Control total = expected artifact count derived from Jira (merged-PR count + fixed set of 3 non-PR artifacts); reconciles against rows extracted from GitHub Enterprise and the CI system with 0 variance.

answers.value: The streaming consumer(s) for the target Kafka topic(s) and their dead-letter topic(s); scope = one pipeline (e.g. policy-events consumer group) processing messages off Azure Event Hubs / Kafka.
Development and test window for the DLQ feature branch, e.g. 2026-06-20 to 2026-07-05, covering unit + integration test runs against a synthetic poison-message set.

Each DLQ record carries: original topic, partition, offset, failure reason, retry count, and first-seen timestamp. Records missing failure reason or offset are themselves alerted as a defect in the handler.
In test: (messages consumed) = (successfully processed) + (routed to DLQ); no message lost or double-counted. Reconciliation over a 10,000-message synthetic batch must balance exactly (delta = 0).

Test results (poison-message routing report, offset reconciliation) stored as CI artifacts in the pipeline run and archived to the source/CI-CD repository release folder with commit SHA and timestamp.

Messages exceeding max-retry (default 3) are routed to the DLQ with disposition metadata; DLQ backlog above threshold raises a monitoring alert and an 'SDLC-Exception' Jira item, owner = Engineering Manager.

Pre/post: replay the synthetic poison-message batch before and after the change; before = messages block/crash the consumer, after = bad messages land in DLQ and good messages continue; comparison report attached to PR.
Change ticket = ServiceNow CHG for the pipeline deployment, linked to the Jira story and the merged GitHub PR delivering the DLQ handler.
Synthetic test set of 10,000 messages including ≥500 crafted poison messages (malformed schema, null keys, oversized payloads) plus valid controls; run in the CI integration stage.
PASS = 100% of poison messages routed to DLQ with correct metadata, 0 valid messages dropped, 0 consumer crashes. FAIL = any poison message reprocessed indefinitely or any valid message lost.

Messages that still cannot be classified route to a secondary quarantine topic and page the on-call via PagerDuty; recurring poison patterns logged as an 'SDLC-Exception' for handler fix within 10 business days.
Test run effective date = CI pipeline run date for the feature branch; results valid for the RC built from that commit only.

Acceptance criteria: (1) all poison messages routed to DLQ with failure metadata; (2) at-least-once delivery preserved for valid messages; (3) DLQ depth metric and alert wired to the service dashboard. Evidence: CI integration-test report + Grafana dashboard link, stored in the GitHub Actions run artifacts and linked on the Jira story.
